subject: VitalCore DPA: runtime ingest clause & subprocessor list - product/security review
messages:
From: Emily Porter <contracts@vitalcore.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft DPA redlines (VitalCore) - runtime ingest & subprocessor ask

Markus / team,

Thanks again for the fast demo last week — the VitalCore team is excited about Redwood’s latency and telemetry controls. Our legal team attached an annotated DPA (VitalCore_DPA_redline_20270620.pdf) with two items we need clarified before we can move to procurement:

1) Runtime ingest for analytics: we requested explicit language that allows VitalCore to receive aggregated / de-identified embeddings generated by the service for our analytics and model-eval pipelines. We flagged a redline in Section 4.3.
2) Subprocessor add: we’re asking that VectorStoreCloud (vectorstore@vendor) be listed as an approved subprocessor for storage and passage of embeddings.

We realize both items touch product/security controls — can you point us to the right contacts at Redwood to confirm technical safeguards (retention, KMS, SOC2 link) and propose updated language? We’ve also attached a brief statement from VectorStoreCloud on their security posture (VectorStoreCloud_subproc_statement.docx).

Can we aim for answers and an updated DPA by end of week? VitalCore is targeting an integration kickoff July 7.

Thanks,
Emily Porter
Senior Counsel, VitalCore Health
attachments: VitalCore_DPA_redline_20270620.pdf, VectorStoreCloud_subproc_statement.docx

Subject: Re: Draft DPA redlines (VitalCore) - runtime ingest & subprocessor ask

Emily — thanks for the note and the redlines. Looping in Lauren (product) and Ben (security) to evaluate impact and propose language. Quick answers up front:

- We can accommodate a narrow \"analytics ingest\" carveout if it is strictly limited to aggregated / irreversible vectors and explicitly excludes raw PII or full request logs.
- VectorStoreCloud as a storage subprocessor is feasible, but security will need their SOC2 report, encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys or equivalent, and an explicit data flow diagram.

Lauren / Ben — two asks for you:
1) Product: can you confirm whether we can implement a scoped runtime export (aggregation-only) for the VitalCore pilot without changing our default telemetry pipeline? If yes, what operational knobs (retention TTL, sampling, hashing) should be in the DPA language?
2) Security: what evidence (reports/attestations) do we need from VectorStoreCloud? Also, what guardrails must be required in the contract (KMS, no model-training, deletion SLA)?

Emily — we’ll reply formally with proposed DPA wording and a short MAP (mutual action plan) by EOD Friday.

—Markus
Markus Klein

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA redlines (VitalCore) - runtime ingest & subprocessor ask

Thanks Markus / Emily — adding product context.

Short answer: we can offer a scoped runtime export for the pilot but need to lock three constraints into the DPA:

- Scope: only embeddings and derived aggregate metrics (no request/response payloads, no trace-level logs).
- Purpose: analytics and model-eval only; explicitly forbid using embeddings to retrain models (no onward model training or derivative model creation).
- Lifecycle: retention TTL configurable per-account (we can offer 7 / 30 / 90 day tiers for the pilot) and an inbound deletion API + documented deletion SLA (48 hours after request).

Operational notes for the team: a) we’ll implement a per-customer toggle that prevents export at any time; b) we should add sampling controls to limit throughput for exports during heavy load; c) we’ll include an annotation prefix to mark exported vectors as \"vitalcore_redacted_v1\" to ensure downstream isolation.

Suggested DPA phrasing (high-level bullet to be refined):
\"Customer may receive aggregated and de-identified embeddings generated by Redwood for the limited purpose of analytics and internal model evaluation. Such embeddings shall not contain raw PII, shall be irreversible, and Customer shall not use them to train third-party models. Retention for exported embeddings shall be limited to the TTL specified in the Order Form and may be deleted on request within 48 hours.\"

I’ll draft a clean paragraph after Ben confirms the security controls required from the subprocessor.

—Lauren Bishop
VP, Product Management
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Emily Porter <contracts@vitalcore.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA redlines (VitalCore) - runtime ingest & subprocessor ask

Appreciate the callouts. Security assessment & minimum evidence needed from VectorStoreCloud:

1) SOC 2 Type II report (latest 12 months) — mandatory.
2) Evidence of encryption at rest and in transit; if VitalCore insists on customer-managed keys (CMK), VectorStoreCloud must support an HSM/KMS integration or provide an equivalent key separation architecture.
3) A binding attestation that VectorStoreCloud will not use embeddings to train any models or combine them with other datasets for re-identification purposes.
4) Data deletion SLA: documented API + runbook and confirmation of deletion within 48 hours after the request (audit log of deletion event).
5) Data flow diagram showing where embeddings are stored, backups, and any live caches.

Contractual guardrails I recommend adding as redline bullets:
- No model training clause for exported vectors.
- Subprocessor must provide annual penetration test summary and a point of contact for incident response.
- Right to audit or receive summarized attestation on security posture as a condition precedent to onboarding.

If VectorStoreCloud cannot meet CMK, propose a mitigated path: limit retention to 7 days and restrict access to a single, tagged bucket with strict IAM. Also suggest we classify this pilot as a "restricted export" for internal ops so we can monitor calls and throttle if abnormal patterns emerge.

Once Emily confirms VectorStoreCloud can provide SOC2 and the attestations, Security can sign off on the subprocessor add. If not, we can propose an alternate approved provider or host the vectors ourselves temporarily (see MAP).

—Ben Carter
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Draft DPA redlines (VitalCore) - runtime ingest & subprocessor ask

Emily — summary and proposed next steps so we have clear alignment: 

1) Product-level carveout: Redwood will support a scoped runtime export for the VitalCore pilot that shares aggregated, irreversible embeddings only (no raw requests or logs). Retention options: 7 / 30 / 90 days (default 30). Deletion SLA: 48 hours. Language to be refined and inserted into Section 4.3.
2) Subprocessor add: VectorStoreCloud can be considered, conditional on: SOC2 Type II (past 12 months), encryption evidence, an explicit non-training attestation, deletion SLA, and a data flow diagram. If VectorStoreCloud cannot provide these artifacts, we will offer a temporary hosting alternative (Redwood-managed bucket with CMK) for the pilot.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for the week:
- VitalCore -> provide VectorStoreCloud SOC2 + attestation + confirmation on CMK or willingness to accept Redwood CMK (by Wed EOD).
- Redwood (Product) -> draft explicit DPA paragraph for 4.3 and a technical appendix describing TTL options (by Thu EOD).
- Redwood (Security) -> confirm required contract language for subprocessor add and prepare a short checklist for procurement (by Thu EOD).
- Both -> Target to have updated DPA and DocuSign envelope ready by Fri close so Procurement can start signature routing next week.

Emily, if that timeline works I’ll drop a redlined paragraph and a short MAP doc into the Drive link and send a DocuSign placeholder.

Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround on this.

—Markus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
